scientific_claim: On two immutable held-out real UTF-8 prose/code files, a bounded pre-degradation calibration monitor corrected the monitor-only failure of the synthetic policy transfer. Across four sequential unknown motif-record deletions, calibration-estimated excess-error ranking selected the true damaged raw-byte motif in every cycle without lesion labels or canonical diagnostic shadow access; every wrong same-budget repair was rejected and reverted, every correct repair exceeded the unchanged 0.20 validation threshold and was retained, and independent audit restored exact canonical predictions, probabilities, and 256-motif structure after every cycle.
program_interpretation: This is the first supported closed-loop Wingless/Yggdrasil maintenance result on naturally distributed errors from immutable real UTF-8 bytes rather than a synthetic grammar. It establishes bounded real-workload detection -> wrong-candidate rejection -> correct repair -> independent validation -> retain -> exact audit recovery for the tested level-1 motif-deletion class. It does not establish open-domain language competence, real second-level hierarchy maintenance, or general autonomous self-repair.
next_question: Generalize the calibrated monitor without retuning across heterogeneous real-byte degradation classes and fresh immutable held-out files; separately attribute the negative real UTF-8 level-2 hierarchy before attempting maintenance at that hierarchy depth.
scope: immutable repo-owned real UTF-8 prose/code level-1 maintenance; four motif-deletion cycles across two files
